entities.summary: Dagobert of Pisa, the first archbishop of Pisa, played a pivotal role in shaping the medieval Christian landscape, particularly in the Holy Land. Born in 1062, Dagobert arrived in Jerusalem in 1107 and was appointed as the second Latin patriarch of the city. This appointment marked a significant turning point in the history of Christian-Jewish relations in the Middle East. Dagobert's tenure was marked by a series of diplomatic efforts to maintain peace between Christians and Muslims, including the establishment of a network of churches and monasteries throughout the region. His legacy extended beyond his own lifetime, influencing the development of Christian institutions in the Holy Land for centuries to come. As the 'Dagobert of Pisa' inscription on the Church of the Holy Sepulchre testifies, his impact on the city's history remains palpable even today.
